job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

response.passage: In the human body, tissues are specialized groups of cells working together to perform specific functions. Many students mistakenly believe that tissues must be solid and fixed in place, but blood is actually a fluid connective tissue that transports oxygen and nutrients throughout the body. Similarly, the idea that we can consciously control every muscle is incorrect; while skeletal muscles are voluntary, cardiac and smooth muscles operate involuntarily to keep our organs functioning without our constant attention. Another common confusion involves the skeletal system. Bones are not dry, non-living structures; they are living tissues rich in blood vessels and cells that constantly remodel themselves. Furthermore, connective tissues like ligaments and tendons are often confused, yet they serve distinct roles: ligaments connect bone to bone, while tendons attach muscles to bones. Finally, epithelial tissue is not restricted to the outer skin. It forms the protective lining of internal organs, blood vessels, and the digestive tract, acting as a barrier for absorption and secretion. Understanding these distinctions is vital for grasping how our body maintains its complex internal environment through division of labour.
response.summary: Tissues are specialized cell groups that perform diverse functions beyond just structural support. This passage clarifies that tissues like blood, bone, and internal linings are living, active components of the human body.
